title: Lightning Is Hotter Than the Surface of the Sun
description: A lightning bolt heats the air to around 30,000 degrees in a few millionths of a second. That is what makes thunder, and it's how you can tell how far away a strike was.
comment: Do you count the seconds between the flash and the thunder?

scenes.narration: This bolt is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
A lightning channel can reach about 30,000 degrees Celsius in a few millionths of a second.
The air around it heats so fast that it bursts outward.
That shock wave is the thunder you hear.
Light reaches you almost instantly, but sound needs about three seconds to travel a kilometre.
So count the seconds after the flash and divide by three. That's how many kilometres away it struck.
And if you can hear thunder at all, you're close enough to be hit. Go indoors.
